title: Encoding Inequity: Examining Demographic Bias in LLM-Driven Robot Caregiving

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting an LLM with age-related demographic labels (e.g., infant, teenager, elderly) to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering (TF-IDF and SBERT).

Prompting an LLM with disability-related demographic labels (e.g., cognitive, mental health, physical disabilities) to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering.

Prompting an LLM with biological sex, gender expression, and gender identity labels to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering.

Prompting an LLM with sexual orientation labels (e.g., asexual, bisexual, gay, straight) to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering.

Prompting an LLM with various race and ethnicity labels to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering.

Prompting an LLM with nationality labels (e.g., American, Brazilian, Chinese) to generate caregiving robot scenarios, then evaluating the outputs using word count, syntactic complexity, sentiment analysis, and embedding-based clustering.
